status.en: 6 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 46% fewer than the week before, most of them in Tigray, Amhara and Oromo.
status.nb: 6 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 46 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Tigray, Amhara og Oromo.

summary.en: Ethiopian and Eritrean forces are massing troops along their shared border and have carried out overnight drone and artillery strikes near Badme, wounding civilians. In southern Ethiopia, clashes between Ethiopian militia and Somali Federalist Party supporters in Moyale have displaced about 700,000 people, prompting the EU to allocate €550,000 emergency aid. A study reports severe disruption to regional healthcare systems and high rates of suicidal behavior among conflict-affected high schoolers. The conflict has caused 2,824 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Etiopiske og eritreiske styrker samler tropper langs den felles grensen og har gjennomført nattlige drone- og artilleriangrep nær Badme, der sivile ble såret. I sørlige Etiopia har sammenstøt mellom etiopisk milits og støttespillere til Somali Federalist Party i Moyale fordrevet omtrent 700 000 personer, noe som har fått EU til å sette av 550 000 € i nødhjelp. En studie rapporterer alvorlig forstyrrelse av regionale helsesystemer og høye forekomster av selvmordstanker blant konfliktpåvirkede videregåendeelever. Konflikten har forårsaket 2 824 dødsfall i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Fano insurgency
background.extract: The Fano insurgency or Amhara war is an armed conflict and insurgency in the Amhara Region of Ethiopia that began in April 2023 between the Fano militia and the Ethiopian government. The conflict started after the government attempted to dissolve the Amhara Special Forces and other regional forces as part of a plan to reform and centralize the country's security apparatus, and integrate them into the federal armed forces. This move led to protests and armed resistance by local forces under Fano.
